question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**literates**" means people who can read and write. (साक्षर)
 
• In the context of the passage, the training courses aim to produce "literates," or individuals who have acquired basic literacy skills.
 
• The other options: "**education**," "**pupils**," and "**beginners**" do not fit as appropriately because "education" is too broad, and "pupils" or "beginners" do not specifically refer to individuals who have gained literacy skills.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *But quite often, what happens is, once the training course is over, to produce literates__, the neo-literates soon lapse into illiteracy.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Education (शिक्षा)**: means a process of receiving or giving systematic instruction. It is too broad for this specific context.
 
• **Pupils (छात्र)**: means students. This term does not specifically refer to individuals who have gained literacy skills.
 
• **Beginners (शुरुआत करने वाले)**: means people who are just starting something. This term is too broad and not specific to literacy.
